text:
From the identity ${cos}^{2}⁡\theta +{sin}^{2}⁡\theta =1,$ with $\theta =3x+2,$ we get 

$$
\begin{aligned}{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3x+2)=1.\end{aligned}
$$

Substituting the above into our integral gives

$$
\begin{aligned}\int \frac{1}{{cos}^{4}⁡(3x+2)+{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2){sin}^{2}⁡(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)({cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)+{sin}^{2}⁡(3x+2))}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int \frac{1}{{cos}^{2}⁡(3x+2)}\,\text{d}x & = \\ \int {sec}^{2}⁡(3x+2)\,\text{d}x & = \\ \frac{1}{3}\operatorname{tan}⁡(3x+2)+C & .\end{aligned}
$$
